reasons.A: Short plain sentences with no contractions fit, but the signposting ('Here is what the window gives me', 'First... Then...') and aphoristic punchlines ('Not speed. Attention.') read as a more didactic, stylised imitation than the author's flat, observational drift.
reasons.B: Long, smoothly subordinated essay sentences, abstract framing ('on paper', 'in practice') and a summarising conclusion are far from the author's clipped fragments and concrete, unexplained close.
reasons.C: Closest movement: terse declaratives and fragments, dry understatement ('It was not free.', 'We do not talk.'), no contractions, concrete sensory lists and short paragraphs; only the closing moral is a touch more explicit than the author.
